articles.title: How a Box of Staples Could Inspire Super-Materials That Assemble and Disassemble on Command
articles.summary: A clump of office staples can behave like a solid block yet fall apart instantly with the right vibration. CU Boulder researchers found staple-shaped particles unlock a rare mix of strength and reversibility, pointing to recyclable construction materials and adaptable robots.

articles.title: NASA's Sharp-Eyed Satellite Catches a Colossal Ocean Swell That Could Unleash El Niño
articles.summary: A massive Kelvin wave—over 5.9 inches above normal sea level—has reached South America, spotted by the Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich satellite. Scientists say it's a key signal that El Niño may develop later this year, with global weather impacts to follow.

articles.title: Drone Tracking Reveals Honey Bees Fly Personal 'Highways' with Centimeter Precision
articles.summary: Using a novel drone-based tracking system, researchers found individual honey bees follow highly consistent flight routes, often within centimeters of previous paths. Landmarks like trees boost accuracy, and the findings challenge old assumptions about the waggle dance's imprecision.
